transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-02 16:00 PDT
Duration: 44 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morris (Redwood AE), Diego Chen (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (QueryCraft - Head of Search), Tom Nguyen (QueryCraft - Eng Manager), Priya Desai (QueryCraft - Data Scientist)

Summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough showing embeddings endpoint and reranking flow; highlighted perf numbers and security controls.

00:00:00 - Lena: hey everyone thanks for joining, we've got about 45 minutes, we'll run through a quick hosted api demo for embeddings and our rerank endpoint and then leave time for q&a
00:00:17 - Sara: sounds great lena, thanks, quick bit of context we get about 200 qps during peak and most queries are fairly short, we also have a mix of recent doc updates so freshness matters
00:00:34 - Tom: also want to understand if we can keep everything in our VPC and tie to our KMS for encryption at rest
00:00:48 - Diego: great, we'll cover that, i'll start by showing the embeddings endpoint, typical request/response, and then the two-stage reranker pipeline we recommend
00:01:05 - Diego: (screen share) here's the hosted embeddings api call, you POST text, we return a vector, you can get different dims depending on model and truncation, note that dims on the demo are 768
00:01:28 - Priya: is that the real model dim or demo mode, we mostly use 512 dims in our infra
00:01:36 - Diego: this is demo model, we support multiple dimensionalities; for your case 512 would be standard, we also show quantized footprints if you want to reduce cost
00:01:52 - Lena: quick note on pricing model: embeddings are billed per embedding unit and rerank is per-token + per-call, we'll send a sample calculator after
00:02:12 - Sara: how do you recommend storing vectors? we currently use elastic for metadata, and pinecone for vectors in a proto setup
00:02:26 - Diego: you can keep metadata in Elastic and use our hosted vectors, or continue with Pinecone; many customers centralize to reduce cross-cloud egress but both patterns work
00:02:47 - Tom: any specific latency numbers for the embedded lookup + rerank path? we're targeting p50 < 100ms for search hits
00:02:59 - Diego: for a typical two-stage flow we see lookup ~20-40ms on an optimized index and rerank (short context) around 80-120ms depending on model; at 200 qps you'd look at dedicated capacity to be predictable
00:03:20 - Sara: can you explain batching? we want to keep latencies low but also control cost, batching seems to trade both
00:03:34 - Diego: yes, we have continuous batching in the runtime that groups small requests, for high qps you can tune target batch size and latency SLO, we can show a demo of queuing and how that affects tail latency
00:03:52 - Priya: how stable are the kernels across models, we have a mix of transformer variants, sometimes k-sparse layers make perf weird
00:04:05 - Diego: good question, our compilation layer selects kernels based on architecture and length distribution, sometimes names get fuzzy in transcripts (k v cache -> kv cache), but we do per-model perf tuning
00:04:24 - Lena: switching to the rerank demo, i'll show a sample pipeline: 1) embed query, 2) vector lookup top N, 3) call rerank model with short context to reorder top N
00:04:44 - Diego: (demo) here i call /embeddings, then call /search which returns ids, then /rerank with the candidate docs and the query, rerank returns scores and best doc id
00:05:10 - Tom: are candidates passed in full text or just ids and we fetch server-side? network cost implications
00:05:22 - Diego: we support both; passing raw text increases token cost but simplifies pipeline, passing ids keeps tokens low but you need the fetch layer; hosted mode can fetch for you if you provide doc store access
00:05:40 - Sara: about data residency, documents stay in region you select, right? we need EU data residency for some customers
00:05:51 - Lena: yes region pinning supported in hosted, and for strict requirements we also have private deployment options with customer-managed VPCs
00:06:09 - Priya: do you have built-in reranking losses or metrics? we run offline metrics and need to see nDCG, MRR etc
00:06:21 - Diego: we provide quality monitoring in the console, you can upload eval sets and we'll compute typical IR metrics, plus regression alerts when score drops
00:06:40 - Sara: can rerank be run as a single api call when you combine lookup and rerank? we'd like a simpler integration if possible
00:06:52 - Diego: you can use our pipeline endpoint which bundles steps but it's effectively the same calls under the hood; bundling has tradeoffs around cacheability and cost
00:07:15 - Lena: quick interjection on security, we support SSO/SAML, role based access, and audit logs; for encryption at rest you can bring your own KMS in private or dedicated
00:07:38 - Tom: curious about burst handling, if we get spikes above 200 qps, is there automatic fallback?
00:07:47 - Diego: our smart routing can fallback to smaller model variants or other regions, and dedicated customers can configure burst pools; fallbacks affect relevance so we recommend profiling with your queries
00:08:05 - Priya: for the benchmark, what sample size do you need? we can provide few thousand queries and set of documents
00:08:13 - Diego: 2k queries and 50k doc snippets is ideal to get meaningful nDCG and latency numbers, that'll be the first action item
00:08:30 - Lena: ok let's walk through an example result, here's a search where baseline returns item A but after rerank we get item C which better matches intent, notice how short context limits token count
00:09:02 - Sara: that looks promising, how do you handle stale docs, do you support incremental reindexing?
00:09:12 - Diego: yes incremental updates supported, and our caching respects TTLs, also you can trigger cache invalidation via API on writes
00:09:30 - Tom: any compliance docs you can share for legal? we need SOC2 and ISO references
00:09:40 - Lena: yes i'll send SOC2 and our security overview, and we have an on-prem/private offering if legal requires air-gapped environments
00:09:56 - Priya: curious about embeddings dimensionality impact on recall, is 512 enough for our domain which has short product titles and synonyms
00:10:08 - Diego: 512 often works well, but we can A/B different dimensions and quantization profiles; Redwood Optimize gives guidance on which profile suits your workload
00:10:30 - Sara: are there customers who've migrated from Pinecone to Redwood? any notes on migration effort
00:10:38 - Lena: yes a few customers migrated and the migration pattern depends on vector store size; we provide scripts and assistance to bulk export/import and to validate via evals
00:10:58 - Tom: about pricing again, can we get example cost at 200 qps with 50k docs and daily reindexing?
00:11:08 - Lena: we'll send a calculator but rough estimate is embedding storage + per-call rerank costs; dedicated pricing flattens per-call costs at scale
00:11:26 - Diego: one more demo note: if you want to reduce token cost on rerank you can send only abstracts or highlights to the reranker and fetch full doc on acceptance, it's a common pattern
00:11:45 - Priya: nice, that would help with cost controls, thanks
00:12:00 - Sara: ok next steps then, we'll send sample data and schedule the benchmark, after results we want a POC scoping call with infra
00:12:12 - Lena: perfect, i'll follow up with the SOW and coordinate dates, thanks everyone
00:12:20 - Meeting end
